post_text:
Metrics lied.

The system was silently dying. 💀

I am a senior engineer; I trust the dashboards. We defined our SLI for the critical background worker as "99th percentile processing latency."

We confidently set the SLO at 500ms.

The dashboard was beautiful. P99 latency stayed flat at 450ms, well within budget. All systems looked green. Success! ✅

But the throughput graph looked jagged. The input queue depth would spike, then immediately drop. I dismissed it as transient network noise.

I assumed P99 latency measured total work completed. It never occurred to me that the metric only tracked successful processing time before the worker gave up.

Weeks later, during an audit, we found 0.5% of daily records stuck in an 'IN_PROGRESS' loop. They weren't failing; they were timing out silently and immediately pulled by another worker.

The latency metric was green because the workers were fast at giving up. The database accumulated stale locks.

The silent cost was four weeks of manual data cleanup for the operations team. 💸

The Moral 👇

A success metric that excludes failure states hides the true cost of data integrity debt.
